hide_of_nemean_lion.name: Hide of the Nemean Lion
hide_of_nemean_lion.unidentified_name: a rough amber pelt of unnatural density
hide_of_nemean_lion.lore: No blade could cut the Nemean Lion, which was the whole point of the first Labour. The arrows of Heracles bounced off it and his club broke on its skull. In the end he cornered it in its cave and strangled it, then found that the only edge able to skin the beast was one of its own claws. He wore the pelt for the rest of his life, its jaws over his head. Steel still slides off it. A hard enough blow still bruises the man inside.

carapace_of_the_hydra.name: Carapace of the Hydra
carapace_of_the_hydra.unidentified_name: a greenish scaled vest that smells faintly of venom
carapace_of_the_hydra.lore: The Hydra of Lerna grew two heads for each one cut away, until Iolaus brought a torch and seared every stump. Heracles dipped his arrows in its gall, and that venom outlived the monster: it wounded the centaur Chiron past healing, killed Nessus, and through the robe Nessus soaked in his own blood it finally killed Heracles. The beast's scales never minded the poison they carried. Whatever bites the wearer learns what was underneath them.

panoply_of_hephaestus.name: Panoply of Hephaestus
panoply_of_hephaestus.unidentified_name: a suit of armour of inhuman precision
panoply_of_hephaestus.lore: Hera threw her son from Olympus because he was born lame. He fell into the sea, where the nymph Thetis hid him nine years, and he came back as the one god the others could not do without. Hephaestus built golden handmaids that could speak and carry, the bronze giant Talos who guarded Crete, and a throne that would not let Hera stand up again. This harness is his own bench work. Smiths who handle it find their own hammers strike truer afterward.

dragon_mail_of_sigurd.name: Dragon-Sewn Mail of Sigurd
dragon_mail_of_sigurd.unidentified_name: a shirt of scale-linked rings with a faint iridescence
dragon_mail_of_sigurd.lore: Sigurd dug a pit in the track the dragon Fafnir took to water and stabbed upward as the worm crawled over him. The German poem, which calls him Siegfried, adds that he bathed in the blood and his skin turned hard as horn, except where a linden leaf had stuck between his shoulder blades. His wife sewed a small cross on his tunic to show a friend where to guard him. Hagen read the mark and put a spear through it.

breastplate_of_joan.name: Breastplate of Joan of Arc
breastplate_of_joan.unidentified_name: a plain breastplate of bare polished steel, cut small
breastplate_of_joan.lore: At seventeen Joan told the Dauphin that God had sent her to raise the siege of Orleans. Charles had a harness of plain polished steel made for her at Tours, the kind armorers called white. At Orleans an arrow went in above her breast; she had it drawn and returned to the wall the same evening, and the English fort fell. Her enemies burned her at Rouen in 1431. The Church struck down the verdict in 1456 and named her a saint in 1920.

lorica_hamata_of_caesar.name: Lorica of Caesar
lorica_hamata_of_caesar.unidentified_name: a fine ring-mail shirt with a faded red hem
lorica_hamata_of_caesar.lore: The lorica hamata was the ringed mail shirt of the legions, and it went with Julius Caesar's armies through eight years in Gaul. He wore no armor to the Senate on the Ides of March. He had dismissed his Spanish bodyguard and ignored the soothsayer Spurinna. The conspirators stabbed him twenty-three times, and the physician Antistius judged that only the second wound, in the chest, was mortal. The mail remembers the day it was left at home and answers the first blade that finds it.

orichalcum_breastplate.name: Orichalcum Breastplate
orichalcum_breastplate.unidentified_name: a chest-piece of reddish-gold metal that vibrates faintly
orichalcum_breastplate.lore: Plato says in the Critias that the kings of Atlantis dug orichalcum out of the earth all over their island, and that only gold was worth more. They sheathed the wall of their inner citadel with it, and it flashed red like fire. Then the sea took the island in a single day and night. Scholars suppose the metal was a kind of brass. Brass does not hum. This breastplate does, and at the top of each slow beat it turns blows aside.

helm_of_hades.name: Helm of Darkness
helm_of_hades.unidentified_name: a dark helm that the eye keeps sliding away from
helm_of_hades.lore: The Cyclopes forged three gifts for the sons of Cronus before the war with the Titans: the thunderbolt for Zeus, the trident for Poseidon, and for Hades a cap that hid its wearer from every eye. Perseus wore it to escape the Gorgon's sisters. Athena put it on at Troy so that Ares would not see who guided the spear into his belly. It hides a man from gods. The dead, who are its owner's subjects, look straight through whoever wears it.

helm_of_achilles.name: Helm of Achilles
helm_of_achilles.unidentified_name: a four-ridged helm with a crest of golden hair
helm_of_achilles.lore: Hector stripped the first armor of Achilles from the body of Patroclus. Thetis went to Hephaestus that night, and by dawn she carried down a new set, the helmet ridged four times and crested with gold. Homer says that when she laid the armor before her son it rang aloud, and the Myrmidons trembled and would not look at it. Only Achilles looked, and his anger grew. The helm has not lost its voice. It sounds at every new threshold.

great_helm_of_galahad.name: Great Helm of Galahad
great_helm_of_galahad.unidentified_name: a white great helm with a small red cross on the cheek
great_helm_of_galahad.lore: Galahad came to Camelot without a shield and sat in the Siege Perilous, the seat that destroyed any knight unworthy of it. Nothing happened. At a white abbey he was given the shield kept for him: white, with a red cross that Joseph of Arimathea's son had drawn in his own blood centuries before. Galahad alone looked into the Grail, and he asked to die in that hour. Nothing foul stays on what he wore. Curses come off the wearer's gear like frost off a window.

vambraces_of_achilles.name: Vambraces of Achilles
vambraces_of_achilles.unidentified_name: a pair of bronze arm-guards worked with tiny farm scenes
vambraces_of_achilles.lore: Homer lists what Hephaestus made for Achilles: a shield, a corselet brighter than fire, a helmet, and greaves of tin. On the shield the god set no battles of heroes. He put two cities, a wedding, a lawsuit, ploughmen, reapers, a vineyard, a dancing floor, and the river Ocean around the rim. These arm-guards are worked in the same hand with the same quiet scenes. They are restful to wear on holy ground, as if the smith wanted his soldier to remember what the fighting was for.

gauntlets_of_mars.name: Gauntlets of Mars
gauntlets_of_mars.unidentified_name: a pair of iron gauntlets engraved with wolf heads
gauntlets_of_mars.lore: The Greeks feared Ares. The Romans loved Mars, who was father to Romulus and had been a god of fields and boundaries before he was a god of war. Farmers prayed to him to keep blight off the wheat. His priests, the Salii, danced through the city each March with the sacred shields, and the campaigning season opened when they finished. The wolf was his animal. These gauntlets are happiest holding a line: a gate, a doorway, the edge of a field.

greaves_of_hermes.name: Greaves of Hermes
greaves_of_hermes.unidentified_name: a pair of bronze greaves, impossibly light, with wings at the ankle
greaves_of_hermes.lore: Greek painters could not agree where the wings of Hermes belonged. Some put them on his sandals, some on his traveler's hat, and some drew them growing from the ankle itself. He needed them. He was herald to Zeus, guide of the dead on the road down to Hades, and the patron of travelers, traders and thieves alike. He stole Apollo's cattle on the day he was born. These bronze shin-guards take the painters' third view, and whoever straps them on finds the world has slowed.

cloak_of_the_morrigan.name: Cloak of the Morrigan
cloak_of_the_morrigan.unidentified_name: a dark feathered cloak that moves without wind
cloak_of_the_morrigan.lore: The Morrigan, the Phantom Queen of the Irish, came to battles as a crow and marked who would fall. She offered Cu Chulainn her love and he refused it. So she attacked him at the ford as an eel, a wolf and a hornless heifer, and he wounded all three. Later he met an old woman milking a cow, blessed her for each of three drinks, and so healed without knowing it the three wounds he had given. On his last day a crow settled on his shoulder.

leggings_of_enkidu.name: Leggings of Enkidu
leggings_of_enkidu.unidentified_name: a pair of rough hide leggings stitched with sinew
leggings_of_enkidu.lore: The goddess Aruru pinched off clay and threw it into the wilderness, and it became Enkidu, shaggy as a beast, who ate grass with the gazelles and tore up the hunters' traps. Shamhat brought him to Uruk. He wrestled King Gilgamesh in the street until the doorposts shook, and the two became brothers. The animals fled from him after that, which grieved him. These leggings are stitched from the wild years. Beasts that walk beside the wearer are harder to kill.

mantle_of_elijah.name: Mantle of Elijah
mantle_of_elijah.unidentified_name: a rough cloak of undyed hair-cloth
mantle_of_elijah.lore: Elijah found Elisha ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen and threw his cloak over him as he passed. Elisha slaughtered the oxen, boiled them over the wood of the plough, fed his neighbors, and followed. Years later a chariot of fire parted them and a whirlwind took Elijah up. The cloak fell. Elisha carried it to the Jordan, struck the water as his master had, and the river divided for him. It is a hairy, undyed thing. Fire has reason to respect it.

robe_of_the_magus.name: Robe of the Magus
robe_of_the_magus.unidentified_name: a deep blue robe with silver astronomical diagrams
robe_of_the_magus.lore: The Magi were the priestly scholars of Persia, readers of stars and dreams. Matthew says that some of them saw a new star rise, followed it west to Jerusalem, and asked King Herod where the child born king of the Jews might be. They found him at Bethlehem and gave gold, frankincense and myrrh. A dream warned them off Herod, and they went home by another road. The silver diagrams on this robe still track the sky, and they reward a mind that studies them.

boots_of_seven_leagues.name: Boots of Seven Leagues
boots_of_seven_leagues.unidentified_name: a pair of worn leather boots that feel ready to move
boots_of_seven_leagues.lore: Charles Perrault wrote them down in 1697. An ogre owned a pair of fairy boots that covered seven leagues at a stride, and he wore them out hunting seven lost brothers. He fell asleep on the rock the boys were hiding under. The smallest, Hop-o'-My-Thumb, pulled the boots off him. They shrank to fit the child, as fairy boots do, and he ran in them to the king's court and made his fortune as a messenger. The pair wears thin slowly. It still wants to go.

brigandine_of_william_wallace.name: Brigandine of Wallace
brigandine_of_william_wallace.unidentified_name: a riveted coat of small iron plates over leather
brigandine_of_william_wallace.lore: William Wallace was the younger son of a small Scottish landholder. In 1297 he and Andrew Moray waited above Stirling Bridge while an English army crossed two riders abreast, then came down and cut the half that had crossed away from the half that had not. He fought from forest and narrow ground for years afterward. Edward I had him executed in London in 1305. This coat of small plates was made for a man who chose his ground, and it likes a tight passage.

cuirass_of_hannibal.name: Cuirass of Hannibal
cuirass_of_hannibal.unidentified_name: a bronze officer's cuirass embossed with a horse and a palm tree
cuirass_of_hannibal.lore: Hannibal Barca brought an army and thirty-seven elephants over the Alps in 218 BC and stayed in Italy fifteen years. At Cannae he let his center bend backward until the Roman mass had pushed deep into a pocket, then closed his African infantry on both flanks and his cavalry on the rear. Some fifty thousand Romans died in an afternoon. He never took Rome, and Scipio beat him at Zama. His cuirass has one habit: it is at its best when the enemy is all around.

aegishjalmr.name: Aegishjalmr
aegishjalmr.unidentified_name: a helm marked on the brow with an eight-armed stave
aegishjalmr.lore: The Helm of Awe lay in the hoard of the dragon Fafnir. Dying, he told Sigurd that he had worn it against all men and that none had dared come near him. Sigurd answered that the helm saves no one once he meets a braver man, and then took it, along with the gold and the cursed ring. Later Icelandic books of magic draw the Helm as a stave of eight branching arms, to be marked on the brow before a fight. It is less a helmet than a sign.

winged_sandals_of_hermes.name: Winged Sandals of Hermes
winged_sandals_of_hermes.unidentified_name: a pair of golden sandals with small live wings at the ankles
winged_sandals_of_hermes.lore: Homer calls them immortal and golden, and says they carried Hermes over the wet sea and the boundless land as fast as the wind blew. He wore them on his father's errands and on the darker road, leading the souls of the dead down to the river. Certain nymphs lent a pair to Perseus, who outflew two Gorgons in them. These are the real thing. The wearer who learns them well stops being where the blow lands.

hermes_sandals_early.name: Hermes's Sandals
hermes_sandals_early.unidentified_name: a pair of plain sandals with small bronze wings riveted on
hermes_sandals_early.lore: The true sandals of Hermes were golden and carried him on the wind between Olympus and the underworld. These are a mortal cobbler's copy, the kind a grateful courier hung on a temple wall after a safe journey. The wings are bronze and the leather is good but ordinary. They kept one trick from the god of travelers and thieves, and only for a moment: the first archer to take aim at the wearer looks the wrong way.

blindfold.name: blindfold
blindfold.lore: Perseus needed a borrowed shield to keep from meeting the Gorgon's eyes. There is a cheaper answer, and this is it: a strip of heavy black cloth, long enough to knot twice. Whoever ties it on sees nothing at all, which is the point, because some things in the dark do their harm through the eyes. Blind men learn to read a floor through their boots. After a while the wearer knows where the nearest footsteps are.

trainers_cap.name: Trainer's Cap
trainers_cap.lore: A well-worn red and white cap, its brim shaped by countless adventures. It radiates a warm, encouraging energy that invigorates companion creatures, helping them recover from wounds more quickly. The inside of the brim reads: 'I choose you.'

cow_kings_horns.name: Cow King's Horns
cow_kings_horns.lore: The gilded horns of the Cow King, pulled from his crowned skull by whoever finally answered the long rumor that there was no such herd and no such king. Worn on the head, they lend a bull's temper: the wearer's first swing lands before the fight has properly begun. The left horn is inscribed with a single word: 'Moo.'

cloth_of_penelope.name: Cloth of Penelope
cloth_of_penelope.lore: Odysseus was gone twenty years, and a hundred and eight suitors moved into his hall to eat his herds until his wife chose one of them. Penelope said she would choose when she finished a burial shroud for old Laertes. She wove at the great loom every day and unpicked the work every night by torchlight, and it held them off for three years. This robe is cut from that cloth. What is torn in it by day is whole again by morning, and so is the wearer.

bracers_of_cu_chulainn.name: Bracers of Cu Chulainn
bracers_of_cu_chulainn.unidentified_name: a pair of battle-scarred leather bracers
bracers_of_cu_chulainn.lore: He was a boy called Setanta when the smith Culann's guard hound came at him. He killed it with his bare hands, and then offered to guard the smith's house himself until a pup could be reared. So men named him Cu Chulainn, the Hound of Culann. In his battle frenzy his body twisted in its skin, one eye sank and the other bulged, and a light rose from his brow. These bracers kept a little of that. The wearer hits harder and minds his own cuts less.

cloak_of_sun_wukong.name: Cloak of Sun Wukong
cloak_of_sun_wukong.lore: Sun Wukong hatched from a stone egg on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. He bullied the Dragon Kings of the four seas out of a golden mail coat, a phoenix-feather cap and cloud-walking boots, ate the peaches of immortality, and fought the armies of Heaven to a standstill. The Buddha shut him under a mountain for five hundred years. He knew seventy-two transformations, and nobody could lay a hand on him twice. The cloak shares the habit. Its wearer is seldom quite where he seems.

coat_of_cu_chulainn.name: Coat of Cú Chulainn
coat_of_cu_chulainn.unidentified_name: a blood-red hide coat that is warm to the touch
coat_of_cu_chulainn.lore: When Queen Medb marched on Ulster to steal the Brown Bull of Cooley, a curse had laid every Ulsterman in his bed. Cu Chulainn was seventeen and exempt. He held the fords alone for months, fighting one champion a day by agreement. This is his war coat. When he was hard pressed the warp-spasm took him, and no army could face what he became. The coat remembers. It wakes when its wearer is nearly dead: strength floods back, pain fades, and the fury takes its own payment.

babr_e_bayan.name: Babr-e Bayan
babr_e_bayan.unidentified_name: a striped tiger-skin coat, unmarked by any blade
babr_e_bayan.lore: Rostam of Zabul is the great champion of the Persian Book of Kings. He rode the horse Rakhsh, who killed a lion while his master slept, and he fought his way through seven trials to kill the White Demon in its cave and free his king. Over his mail he wore the Babr-e Bayan, a coat of tiger skin that neither fire nor water nor any weapon could spoil. In each new place the first blow that reaches it is simply refused.

tarnhelm.name: Tarnhelm
tarnhelm.unidentified_name: a dull helm of fine iron mesh
tarnhelm.lore: In the old German poem Siegfried wins a cloak of darkness from the dwarf Alberich, keeper of the Nibelung hoard. Wagner turned it into a helm of fine mesh, forged by the smith Mime on his brother Alberich's orders, and Alberich used it to walk unseen among his own people with a whip. The giant Fafner later wore it to take the shape of a dragon. It still hides its wearer completely, though only for a few breaths, and then it must rest.

linothorax_of_alexander.name: Linothorax of Alexander
linothorax_of_alexander.unidentified_name: a stiff cuirass of layered white linen
linothorax_of_alexander.lore: The great mosaic found at Pompeii shows Alexander charging the Persian king bareheaded, in a corselet of stiff layered linen with a Gorgon's face on the chest. Plutarch says that at Gaugamela he wore a doubled linen breastplate taken from the spoils of Issus. Linen armor was cooler than bronze and lighter on a long march, and enough layers will stop an arrow. His phalanx marched from Greece to India. A soldier who rests in it on holy ground mends quickly.

coif_of_beowulf.name: Coif of Beowulf
coif_of_beowulf.unidentified_name: a riveted iron coif with small boar figures on the brow
coif_of_beowulf.lore: Grendel carried no sword, so Beowulf put his own aside and waited in the dark hall of Heorot. He caught the monster's arm and held on until it tore loose at the shoulder, and the Danes hung it under the roof. The poem describes his helmet as banded by a smith of old and set with boar figures so that no blade could bite. In 1939 a ship burial at Sutton Hoo gave up a helmet with boars at the brow. Nothing keeps hold of this coif's wearer for long.

sandals_of_perseus.name: Sandals of Perseus
sandals_of_perseus.unidentified_name: a pair of worn fisherman's sandals with bronze buckles
sandals_of_perseus.lore: Perseus grew up on the island of Seriphos in the house of a fisherman, after the sea washed him and his mother ashore in a wooden chest. At a feast he boasted that he would fetch the king the Gorgon's head, and the king held him to it. These are what he had on his feet when he set out: plain leather with bronze buckles. The winged pair came later, on loan. A hero starts walking before the gods lend him anything.

kilt_of_the_pharaoh.name: Kilt of the Pharaoh
kilt_of_the_pharaoh.unidentified_name: a pleated linen kilt shot with gilt thread
kilt_of_the_pharaoh.lore: The shendyt was the royal kilt of Egypt for three thousand years: fine linen wrapped at the hips, pleated sharp, with a tapering panel in front. Sculptors carved it on every pharaoh from the pyramid builders to Cleopatra's line. Howard Carter found heaps of folded linen in Tutankhamun's tomb, kilts and tunics and more than a hundred loincloths, all dry as paper. A king was buried with his wardrobe because he meant to need it. What is lost with this kilt on is not lost for good.

scale_of_dilmun.name: Scale of Dilmun
scale_of_dilmun.unidentified_name: a bronze scale shirt, green at the edges, smelling of salt
scale_of_dilmun.lore: The Sumerians told of Dilmun, a pure bright land in the sea toward the sunrise, where the raven did not croak and the lion did not kill. It had no fresh water until the god Enki called springs up from under the earth. After the flood the gods settled Ziusudra there, the one man they let live forever. Most scholars place Dilmun on the island of Bahrain, where sweet springs still rise through salt water. This bronze shirt is at home wherever water stands.

helm_of_gilgamesh.name: Helm of Gilgamesh
helm_of_gilgamesh.unidentified_name: a beaten gold war helm shaped like braided hair
helm_of_gilgamesh.lore: Leonard Woolley dug the Royal Cemetery of Ur in the 1920s and lifted out a helmet beaten from a single sheet of gold alloy, shaped like a wig with every curl and the knot of hair at the back chased into the metal. It belonged to a man named Meskalamdug. The Sumerian King List gives Gilgamesh a reign at nearby Uruk, and his epic was old before Babylon was great. A king's helm expects tribute. Gold offered to it is not wasted.

sandals_of_theseus.name: Sandals of Theseus
sandals_of_theseus.unidentified_name: a pair of weathered leather sandals with bronze studs
sandals_of_theseus.lore: King Aegeus hid a sword and a pair of sandals under a boulder at Troezen and told the mother that the boy could come to Athens when he was strong enough to lift it. Theseus lifted it at sixteen and took the land road, which was the dangerous one. He bent Sinis between his own pine trees, kicked Sciron off his own cliff, and fitted Procrustes to his own iron bed. The sandals learned the lesson on that road. They return harm in the shape it arrives.

greaves_of_qin.name: Greaves of the Qin Guard
greaves_of_qin.unidentified_name: a pair of lacquered leather greaves stamped with seal script
greaves_of_qin.lore: The First Emperor of Qin was buried in 210 BC with an army of fired clay to guard him: some eight thousand soldiers, no two faces alike, standing in battle order in pits a mile from his tomb. Farmers digging a well found them in 1974. The sculptors copied the real armor plate by plate, small squares of lacquered leather laced with cord. Lacquer sheds water and stiffens the hide beneath it, and very little eats through it. The seal on these names the workshop foreman.

cloak_of_odin.name: Wanderer's Cloak of Odin
cloak_of_odin.unidentified_name: a deep blue traveler's cloak with one missing eyelet
cloak_of_odin.lore: Odin gave one eye to Mimir's well for a drink of wisdom, and afterward he walked the world as an old man in a blue cloak and a hat pulled low on that side. He called himself Grimnir, or Gangleri, or Vegtam. He asked for a seat by the fire, traded riddles with kings and giants, and left before anyone thought to count his eyes. His ravens Huginn and Muninn brought him the news each morning. The cloak has the same hunger to know what things are.

bracers_of_arjuna.name: Bracers of Arjuna
bracers_of_arjuna.unidentified_name: a pair of engraved leather archer's bracers with brass studs
bracers_of_arjuna.lore: Arjuna was the finest archer among the five Pandava brothers, and he could draw the bow Gandiva with either hand. On the morning of the battle of Kurukshetra he saw his teachers and cousins in the opposing line and let the bow slip from his fingers. His charioteer was Krishna. What Krishna told him between the two waiting armies fills eighteen chapters, and it is called the Bhagavad Gita. Arjuna picked up the bow. The first arrow a wearer looses in a new place flies with that settled mind.

girdle_of_hippolyta.name: Girdle of Hippolyta
girdle_of_hippolyta.unidentified_name: a braided leather war-girdle with a bronze clasp
girdle_of_hippolyta.lore: Ares gave his daughter Hippolyta, queen of the Amazons, a war belt as the sign of her command. Heracles was sent to fetch it for a princess of Mycenae as his ninth Labour. Hippolyta came down to his ship and offered it freely. Then Hera, in the shape of an Amazon, ran through the camp crying that the stranger was carrying off the queen. The riders charged, and Heracles killed her believing himself betrayed. The belt still answers a straight, gathering charge.

helm_of_leonidas.name: Helm of Leonidas
helm_of_leonidas.unidentified_name: a Corinthian bronze helm with a crest set ear to ear
helm_of_leonidas.lore: A Persian scout rode up to the pass at Thermopylae and found the Spartans stripped for exercise and combing their long hair. Xerxes laughed at the report. An exiled Spartan king in his camp explained that these men dressed their hair when they meant to risk their lives. Leonidas held the pass two days, sent most of the allies home on the third, and died with his three hundred. His helm does its best work when its wearer is nearly finished.

cloak_of_mulan.name: Cloak of Mulan
cloak_of_mulan.unidentified_name: a heavy red wool cloak with frost-line patterns
cloak_of_mulan.lore: The Ballad of Mulan dates from the age of the Northern Wei. The Khan's draft scroll carried her father's name, and he had no grown son. She bought a horse in the east market, a saddle in the west, a bridle in the south and a whip in the north, and rode in his place for ten years of frontier war. Her comrades did not know her in a dress. On holy ground the cloak lets the wearer put the soldier down and rest.

haramaki_of_yoshitsune.name: Haramaki of Yoshitsune
haramaki_of_yoshitsune.unidentified_name: a cuirass of small lacquered plates laced with dark red silk
haramaki_of_yoshitsune.lore: In 1184 the Taira held a fortress at Ichi-no-Tani with the sea in front and a cliff behind. Minamoto no Yoshitsune watched deer pick their way down the cliff, reasoned that a horse could follow where a deer went, and led a handful of riders straight down onto the rear of the camp. A year later he destroyed the Taira fleet at Dan-no-ura. His brother the shogun grew afraid of him and hunted him to death. The armor still quickens on every descent.

boots_of_thor.name: Iron Boots of Thor
boots_of_thor.unidentified_name: a pair of heavy iron boots scarred by lightning
boots_of_thor.lore: Snorri counts three treasures of Thor: the hammer, the belt of strength, and the iron gloves he needed to grip the hammer. No poet lists his boots. Yet Thor was the one god who could not ride the rainbow bridge, which would have burned under him, so he waded four rivers every day to reach the judgment seat by the World Tree. He forded Vimur while a giantess swelled the flood. Whatever he wore on his feet did that. Sparks jump from these when enemies crowd close.

helm_of_aragorn.name: Helm of the King Returned
helm_of_aragorn.unidentified_name: a winged silver helm with a pale gem in the brow
helm_of_aragorn.lore: Tolkien describes the crown of Gondor as a tall white helm with wings of pearl and silver like a gull's and seven gems set in the circlet. It waited in a king's tomb through the long rule of the stewards. The man who claimed it had spent most of his life as a ranger called Strider. To reach his city in time he took the Paths of the Dead and called an army of oathbreakers to keep their word at last. The dead still listen to this helm.

robes_of_solomon.name: Robes of Solomon
robes_of_solomon.unidentified_name: a robe of gold thread embroidered with rows of strange names
robes_of_solomon.lore: Solomon's wisdom was the gift he asked for when God offered him anything. The wealth and the long reign came as a bonus. Late tradition gave him a signet ring that commanded the demons; the embroidered names on his robes were said to be theirs. The Temple he built was destroyed twice. The Wisdom literature attributed to him survives. The robes are what wisdom looks like when it has been embroidered for the throne room.

armor_of_ragnarok.name: Armor of Ragnarök
armor_of_ragnarok.unidentified_name: an iron-and-bone harness scarred by old burns
armor_of_ragnarok.lore: Ragnarök is the doom of the gods. Odin dies in the wolf's mouth. Thor kills the world-serpent and walks nine steps before falling from its venom. The world burns and sinks and rises again with a smaller pantheon and a memory of what happened. This is the harness for the day the gods knew was coming and went out to meet anyway. The Norse called that courage, not despair.

crown_of_brahma.name: Crown of Brahma
crown_of_brahma.unidentified_name: a four-tiered golden crown that hums with mantra
crown_of_brahma.lore: Brahma woke on a lotus that grew from the navel of sleeping Vishnu, and from his thought came the worlds. The Puranas say he grew a face for each quarter of the sky so that nothing he had made could pass out of his sight, and that from his four mouths came the four Vedas. He rides a white goose and carries a water pot and a string of prayer beads, never a weapon. His crown has a tier for each face. Its wearer is not easily approached from behind.

duck_of_doom.name: Duck of Doom
duck_of_doom.lore: You should know better than to pick up a duck in a dungeon.
